lead: Corporate platforms, learning products, marketplaces and storefronts — shipped, live and in use. Each one with the problem it solved and how.

closing.body: Tell me what you're building. The contact details are right below.

waco.challenge: An industrial and engineering consultancy in Riyadh needed a site that worked first in Arabic, read just as well in English and Chinese, and could be updated by its own team without a developer.
waco.approach: An Arabic-first, right-to-left Next.js front end with full English and Chinese, light and dark themes, two structured lead forms, and a Filament admin over Laravel where the team manages services, projects, partners, people, the blog, news and testimonials.
waco.outcome: One site in three languages that the WACO team runs themselves: new projects, news and testimonials go live from the admin, with no code changes.

teryaq.challenge: Medical students needed one place to study: structured courses, question banks to practise on, and a clear view of their own progress.
teryaq.approach: A Next.js platform with courses, question banks and progress tracking, a full admin panel for the content team, and automatic deploys that check the new release and roll back on their own if it isn't healthy.
teryaq.outcome: A live learning platform the team can grow without touching code, shipping updates safely on every change.

khidmty.challenge: Booking a reliable electrician, plumber, carpenter or painter usually means calls, guesswork and a sign-up form before you even see who's available.
khidmty.approach: A bilingual Arabic/English marketplace where every professional is manually verified, and customers can book without creating an account.
khidmty.outcome: A shorter path from need to booking, with trust built in through verification rather than reviews alone.

civicmind.role: Frontend development, in an AI Week team
civicmind.challenge: Citizen reports reach municipalities unsorted, so someone has to read each one to decide what it is, who handles it and how urgent it is.
civicmind.approach: A civic platform where citizens file reports and trained models classify the category, the responsible department and the urgency.
civicmind.outcome: Reports arrive already sorted and routed, so staff start with the most urgent issues instead of the inbox.

onyx.challenge: Most storefronts break the browsing rhythm: every product click and cart action feels like a full stop.
onyx.approach: A storefront built around motion, with product transitions and cart interactions designed to carry the shopper from one step to the next.
onyx.outcome: Browsing that flows: the motion explains where you are and what just happened, instead of decorating the page.

saleh.challenge: A graphic designer's portfolio has to show the work, not compete with it.
saleh.approach: A restrained site where layout, type and motion step back and let each project lead.
saleh.outcome: A portfolio the work can speak through, built to be fast and easy to browse.

eyad.challenge: A professional designer needed a portfolio and services site he could keep current himself.
eyad.approach: A portfolio and services site structured so new work and services can be added without a developer in the loop.
eyad.outcome: A site that stays up to date because updating it is easy.
